query: For reported HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure, what testable hypothesis could enable Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior to be predicted more rapidly and accurately under tensile and fracture testing than with established simulations? State the hypothesized rationale, the measurable gains in predictive accuracy and efficiency, circumstances in which the hypothesis may fail, relevant supporting evidence, and a predeclared result from independent measurements that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating DFT‐calculated pairwise interaction features with explicit descriptors of the hierarchical heterostructure (e.g. nanoprecipitate distributions and grain-boundary characteristics) into a machine learning framework will enable more rapid and accurate predictions of Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10 compared to conventional continuum or empirical simulations.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk HfNbTiVAl10 as fabricated in its as-cast state with a reported hierarchical heterostructure (including intragranular nanoprecipitates and distinct grain-boundary features).
generation.intervention: Develop and apply a multiscale modeling approach that combines DFT-derived atomic interaction data with microstructural parameters as inputs to an ML model, then use this surrogate model to predict tensile and fracture properties under standardized mechanical testing conditions.
generation.conditions: Tensile and fracture tests conducted at room temperature under controlled strain rates; simulation comparisons made against established finite element or empirical prediction methods applied to similarly processed HfNbTiVAl10 samples.
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchical microstructure features (e.g. spatial distribution and size of nanoprecipitates, grain-boundary defect density) that mediate the link between local atomic interactions (from DFT pair interaction calculations) and macroscopic mechanical behavior.
generation.mechanism: Local atomic bonding characteristics influence interfacial energies and defect formation within the hierarchical heterostructure. When integrated via ML, these descriptors capture the complex interplay between nanoscale heterogeneities and macroscopic properties, thereby enabling a more efficient and quantitative prediction of mechanical responses under load.
generation.predicted_outcome: The proposed predictive framework is expected to improve the accuracy of predicted Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional simulation approaches, and reduce computational prediction time by roughly an order of magnitude.
generation.baseline: Existing continuum or empirical simulation methods that generally do not account explicitly for DFT-derived atomic interaction details or the full complexity of hierarchical heterostructuring, resulting in longer simulation times and lower accuracy.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis may fail if the actual microstructural features (such as unexpected processing-induced defects or phase anomalies) deviate significantly from those characterized and assumed in the model, or if the DFT-derived interaction parameters do not accurately capture real atomic behavior in this specific alloy system.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvements in predictive accuracy and efficiency are uncertain until the model is validated against extensive experimental datasets; additionally, variability in microstructural characterization may influence prediction reliability.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a set of HfNbTiVAl10 samples with verified hierarchical heterostructures. Conduct standardized tensile and fracture tests to measure Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness. Independently, use the integrated ML-DFT framework to predict these mechanical properties under the same conditions. Compare the predictions with experimental measurements and record computational time for both approaches.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML-DFT model produces predictions with a relative error greater than 25% for any key mechanical property and/or achieves less than a twofold reduction in simulation time compared to established simulation methods, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

Predicting Yield Strength and Plastic Elongation in Body-Centered Cubic High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: We employ machine learning (ML) to predict the yield stress and plastic strain of body-centered cubic (BCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) in the compression test. Our machine learning model leverages currently available databases of BCC and BCC+B2 entropy alloys, using feature engineering to capture electronic factors, atomic ordering from mixing enthalpy, and the D parameter related to stacking fault energy. The model achieves low Root Mean Square Errors (RMSE). Utilizing Random Forest Regression (RFR) and Genetic Algorithms for feature selection, our model excels in both predictive accuracy and interpretability. Rigorous 10-fold cross-validation ensures robust generalization. Our discussion delves into feature importance, highlighting key predictors and their impact on mechanical properties. This work provides an important step toward designing high-performance structural high-entropy alloys, providing a powerful tool for predicting mechanical properties and identifying new alloys with superior strength and ductility.

Integrated design of aluminum-enriched high-entropy refractory B2 alloys with synergy of high strength and ductility

Abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are promising high-temperature structural materials. Their large compositional space poses great design challenges for phase control and high strength-ductility synergy. The present research pioneers using integrated high-throughput machine learning with Monte Carlo simulations supplemented by ab initio calculations to effectively navigate phase selection and mechanical property predictions, developing single-phase ordered B2 aluminum-enriched RHEAs (Al-RHEAs) demonstrating high strength and ductility. These Al-RHEAs achieve remarkable mechanical properties, including compressive yield strengths up to 1.7 gigapascals, fracture strains exceeding 50%, and notable high-temperature strength retention. They also demonstrate a tensile yield strength of 1.0 gigapascals with a ductility of 9%, albeit with B2 ordering. Atomic Interaction-Based Prediction of Phase Formations in High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are of particular interest due to their unique combination of high strength, ductility, and fracture resistance. These properties are largely impacted by the phases and number of phases present in the alloy. Due to the enormous chemical design space, with typically five or six elements present in the alloys in addition to the various processing parameters, the prediction of the number of phases is challenging. While there have been multiple recent reports of phase predictions through data-driven models, an alternate approach is proposed and demonstrated here. In this work, phase prediction is performed using features derived from DFT-calculated pairwise interactions among constituent elements (incorporating bonding and structure) rather than relying solely on traditional elemental descriptors such as electronegativity. By focusing on atomic interaction features, our model provides a novel perspective on the phase stability in HEAs. A high-entropy alloy with hierarchical nanoprecipitates and ultrahigh strength

Abstract: HEAs’ compositional space allows the design of hierarchical microstructures that contribute to the exceptional strength values. AbstractHigh-entropy alloys (HEAs) are a class of metallic materials that have revolutionized alloy design. They are known for their high compressive strengths, often greater than 1 GPa; however, the tensile strengths of most reported HEAs are limited. Here, we report a strategy for the design and fabrication of HEAs that can achieve ultrahigh tensile strengths. The proposed strategy involves the introduction of a high density of hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates. To establish the validity of this strategy, we designed and fabricated a bulk Fe25Co25Ni25Al10Ti15 HEA to consist of a principal face-centered cubic (fcc) phase containing hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates.
